utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning to you all. Welcome back, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was informed that you had something to raise before we begin today's business.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you very much. It involves the time for the interview of General Abdel-Razek, who is supposed to be testifying on Monday. And the UNDU has indicated that they would not accommodate an interview over the weekend with him, and they are proposing a Friday-evening interview, which means that tomorrow Dr. Karadzic would be cross-examining or be involved in the court from 9.00 to 3.00, and they would want the interview from 4.00 until 7.00. And we're simply not prepared for the interview, unfortunately, under those circumstances, so we were going to ask if the Chamber could possibly sit on Monday afternoon instead of the schedule of 9.00 to 3.00 so that we could conduct the interview Monday morning between 9.00 and 12.00, in which time we could prepare for it over the weekend. Given the pace of the trial, we think that it's really not reasonable to require Dr. Karadzic to interview a witness on the Friday evening when he's been cross-examining for the last two weeks. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are sitting 9.00 to 2.30 tomorrow. That's one thing. And I will inquire with all the staff involved whether it would be possible to sit from 1.30 to 7.00 on Monday, again three 90-minute sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you have --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't have an objection, in principle, but I am not aware of the particular circumstances of the witness. So now that this is on the table, I will inquire of the relevant participants and see if we have any useful -- any significant feedback for the Court in regard to this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we hear the responses from parties and the Registry as to the feasibility of sitting from 1.30 to 7.00 by the end of today's session. Well, let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mandic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, let's continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning to all. Could I please have in e-court 65 ter 01588.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Minister, this is going to be a very brief survey of one of a series of documents dealing with a topic that we touched upon yesterday. Can you please have a look at this. It's the 19th of July. From the level of the ministry, this is what's being done -- or, actually, why don't you explain this to us. The conclusions of the minister of the interior are being elaborated and sent further down. Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was sent from the ministry to all centres, and there were five of them in Republika Srpska; namely, Banja Luka, Bijeljina, Doboj, Sarajevo and Trebinje. The objective of this communication is to resolve the question of jurisdiction between the police and the Army of Republika Srpska; also to deal with certain problems related to the activity of paramilitary formations in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina or, rather, Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the second paragraph and the first sentence under A.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A. Problems related to the activities of some paramilitary units, especially in cases where crimes have been committed or the public peace and order violated to a large extent, the problems of joint command and conflicts with authorities, positive or negative connotations in psychological/propaganda terms, the possibility of confrontation and other relevant information - as well as suggestions as to what measures could be applied to resolve the problems."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So it says up here that it had been agreed that security services would submit data. Could you just read the first sentence of subparagraph B?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Data and information regarding police involvement in those combat actions when their involvement is necessary."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page. I believe it's the next page in English too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, since these are documents that are being sent to the ground and sometimes can be rather imprecise, let us see what V says, and then we'll see what G says in relation to civilians.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "V. Problems related to the prevention/detection of crimes and perpetrators. The functioning of combined check-points; the seizure of vehicles on the grounds that they have been acquired or registered illegally; the defence of borders; professional activities, combat support," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have a look at G. What kinds of persons does it deal with?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Procedures and jurisdiction; the treatment and custody of prisoners, persons evacuated from the combat operation zones; collection camps into which the army brings Muslim residents without any documents that might state reasons for such action, and then leave these undefined camps to the organs of the interior." What they're saying is the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Isn't it clear here that if the military is carrying out a particular action, and then they take the civilian population from the combat area and put them up somewhere?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, actually, I can read this too: "Work of the military judiciary --" All of this can be read out, but finally it says that: "The dead-line is the 25th of July, 1992." Mr. Stanisic, minister of the interior, signed this; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this document was written on the 19th of July and the dead-line is the 25th, that is to say, there was a seven-day dead-line to operate on the basis of these conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Minister, are you aware of a single case of a different type of rounding up the civilian population, except for the case with combat zones?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any other case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this in line with the commander -- with the order of the commander of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps that civilians should not be sent to barracks, to him, but that the civilians should be sent elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is in line with what Cedo Sladojevic, the chief of staff of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, concluded.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D450.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1D208. It is also 1D3012.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the previous document, we saw that there are some conflicts, that there is an overlap in authority and in carrying out one's duties?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and disobedience at local level, vis-a-vis the central authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This document -- well, I don't know if we have a translation. That is what it deals with, so this is what I'd like to ask you -- no, no, this is not it. This is -- no, no, the previous document, the previous one. Yes, that's fine in Serbian. Can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has to do with a clash between the military police and the civilian police in Drvar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it says here that around 9.30 p.m. --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Around 9.30 p.m., 30 policemen, military policemen of the 2nd Corps, attacked the Public Security Station of Drvar. Probably it had to do with some coffee bars and description of law and order. That is what led to these clashes between the police and the military police; that is to say, between the army and the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read out this paragraph: "On the occasion of this attack ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the occasion of these attacks, members of the military police threatened that they would have a show-down with the police; that they would attack the Public Security Station; that they would mistreat the police on different roads, and that Zoljas would be flying at the station; that they would expel the police from Drvar; and that the police had allegedly declared war on the military police."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a constant danger, that there can be no coexistence between two armed formations in a single area without sparks flying?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was a conflict between two armed forces, and that was a major problem.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D451, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have D95. This has already been admitted. It is also 1D206, but D95 certainly has a translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, this is my reaction to some of the things that were happening again in the municipalities of Birac and Stari Herzegovina. These municipalities listed here, are they in that area?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Gorazde, Foca, Han Pijesak, Sokolac, Rogatica, Visegrad, Rudo and Cajnice. That's the area of Old Herzegovina, Stari Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me what it is that I am ordering here?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are ordering all these municipalities here that all the villages in which the Croat and Muslim population surrender their weapons, and state that they do not intend to fight against us, must enjoy full protection from our Serb state of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The presidents of municipalities will be held accountable for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, do you remember that General Mladic on several occasions asked for their disarming and have them turn into civilians? Unfortunately, there is a mistake in the translation here. Instead of "disarm" it says "surrender." Do you make a distinction between the two, yourself?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To disarm means to hand over weapons, whereas to surrender means that someone will be arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This document has been admitted, so we don't have to admit it now. But we're dealing with that topic, how the civilian population is being treated, even those who had been fighting and that are supposed to give up fighting?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have D92. That has also been admitted. It's an Assembly session held on the 24th and 26th of July, 1992. Once we've identified it, can we move on to 13 in Serbian and page 17 in English; in the document itself, that is, 13th page in the document itself, and it's actually page 14 in e-court. So one up in Serbian. Yes, and page 17 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is part of my speech. I'd like to draw the attention of the participants to this paragraph in the middle that says: "I must say that the Serb people ...," et cetera. I'll continue in Serbian: "I must say that the Serb people, whose Orthodox nature has kept them far from being inhumane, have found a number of traitors among themselves ..." Can you explain what a traitor is? I don't know what the translation was.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People who do not have the characteristics of their own people, and in a negative context, at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. "Traitor" is the word used here in the translation, but the word "izrod" is even worse. It means does not even belong to one's own people, one's own kin. It does not have the same characteristics at all. So, further on it says: "... inhumane people who are committing inhumane acts, ones that we shall try and punish by law." Do you agree that that's what the first paragraph states or, rather, this paragraph in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Further on, it says: "From the most severe acts to the smallest, the most severe acts are the rarest, while the smallest ones are the most frequent, statistics show: robbery, unlawful acquiring of property, et cetera, all of that is a consequence of a terrible war, the most horrible among civil wars. In essence, it is not a civil war, because this is an inter-ethnic and religious war. I can say that the Serbs have stayed so far away from the property of others, especially property belonging to members of other nations and ethnic groups. War has changed some people so much that there are individuals among them who are very keen on other people's property, both Muslim and Serb property. Here we have great political problems. It is an immense blow to our soldiers' morale, which is otherwise excellent, but in any case what hurts them are the robberies and crimes being committed behind their backs while they are fighting." Was that our position throughout that war of ours?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us about this other paragraph: "One of the essential problems ...," et cetera? Since you were the minister of justice, this is a topic you're familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You spoke with the problem of how the central authorities functioned. They were in isolation, and the autonomous regions had power in their own hands, and, in a way, they were alienated from the central authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "We will all know immediately that ..." Could you read it, actually?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then you said: "That people will then know that this is a proper Serb tendency of insisting on autonomy, creating small princely states with small princes in them."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you finish that? Can you read it to the end?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "There is a private interest behind them, invariably, rather than the interest of the people."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have page 15 in Serbian and page 19 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the middle, where it says: "To the Presidency and the government ...," and then it goes on to say: "At this stage --" let's see: "At this stage --" let's see where it is in English. Just a moment. Let me see if we have the correct page in English: "At this stage," the bottom half, "Presidency and government -- at this stage, the priority," you can find this?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At this stage, the priority is to introduce order in the state mechanisms of power, that is, the state organs; reorganising the police for peacetime; placing the remaining police force within the JNA; placing all the special police, which are being misused by some, under the single command of the republic MUP, not under the command of local lords."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Is this the problem in self-managing socialism, where the local -- the local authorities had too much power in relation to the central authorities?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page in Serbian, please, and in English also. It's page 20 in English. I must tell you that according to the law and international law, everything enacted by various crisis staffs and war presidencies are measures adopted in wartime conditions and are not legal in the way they would be if enacted by the local -- by the government authorities.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's at the top of the page in Serbian. Let's see it in English. Where is it in English: "I must say --" it's around a third of the way down: "I must say that, therefore, the Assembly recommends that what the Presidency has decided, enacting as the Assembly, to set up the legally-elected organs of authority, civilian authorities, which should not function as the military authority's rival, but as their partner. Most importantly, one must effectively eliminate para-state and also paramilitary formations. The para-state ones at this stage are even more dangerous, because they can make catastrophic decisions that nobody would even recognise in peacetime, but only cause us great damage in the meantime."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the Presidency here is offering its decisions, which if enacted on behalf of the Assembly, for the Assembly to adopt and confirm?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that in the transcript, it says that the Presidency is offering its decisions which it enacted on behalf of the Assembly for the Assembly to confirm, because this is the obligation of the Presidency to tender its decisions to the Assembly at the first opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the right interpretation, the one I have just given?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Verification or confirmation of your decisions was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can it be seen here that the state organs or the Presidency is informing the Assembly that the para-state organs that have sprung up are even more dangerous than the paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, you highlighted the problem of the paramilitary formations and the crisis staffs which usurped power, so this was an armed force which was not under the control of any state organs or the army, and the local authorities which were not under the control of the Government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the same page, it says that in Bosnia -- so Karadzic is still speaking: "In Bosnia-Herzegovina, no one -- because nobody in Bosnia-Herzegovina --" It's the beginning of the last third of the page, the bottom third, and it's in the middle of the page in Serbian: "... nobody in Bosnia-Herzegovina has legal organs of government, apart from the Serbs, and to trace several paths to further entrench the state and build its first, second, and third floors -- to further entrench the state and build its first, second, and third floors, so we could walk towards the roof of this state house ..." And then it goes on to state lower down: "The government organs must be energetic in implementing everything that has been envisioned and that is of a formative character, building up the state." Was this the constant concern of the government organs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 17 to 18 in Serbian, where Mr. Djeric is speaking. We already have the page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djeric says: "It is well known that the Government of the Serbian Republic of BiH began constituting itself and working in wartime conditions of the most brutal kind." The next page in English. Next page in English, please: "The government started its work in a complete state of isolation. It was cut off from all sources of communication, ranging from available institutions, services, functions, information, means of equipment, technology and staff." Is this in accordance with what you know about the status of the government and the conditions in which it worked?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we spoke about this here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So although you had certain misunderstandings with Mr. Djeric, you agree in what he says -- you agree with what he says here?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have page -- the next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The government, because of the war -- it's a third of the way down the page.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Namely, at the very beginning of its work, the government was involved in issuing regulations, setting up the system, and creating the legal prerequisites for the organisation and work of the state organs, business enterprises, social activities, and all the other preconditions for the functioning of the new Serbian state."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you go on to where it says: "Namely, fighting and other factors ..." Let's see where it is in English.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Namely, fighting and other factors have kept the government fully isolated from municipalities for a long period of time."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that Mr. Djeric goes on to discuss this further. Milanovic also speaks about this, so throughout this transcript we can see this. This has already been admitted into evidence. So this is the second half of July, and we are still having problems of the same nature as in April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 65 ter 191.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In some parts of the indictment, it has been suggested that the SDS centralised power in Republika Srpska, with the intention of implementing its criminal intent more easily, and the whole indictment hangs on the alleged intent to remove Croats and Muslims from the territories claimed by the Serbs. Are these minutes from a government session held on the 29th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the "1st of August" in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the subtitle?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The minutes were drawn up on the 1st of August, but the session was held on the 29th of July, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next two pages, AD-1, both in English and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you say, Minister, that the government tried to centralise the government administration in order to carry out what is mentioned in the indictment, or did it do so in order to prevent what was mentioned in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the government tried to centralise power because on the ground there were certain breaches of the law, serious ones, especially in relation to the non-Serb population. So we saw that at the proposal of the government, the crisis staffs were abolished. After that, the autonomous regions were disbanded. And these local warlords that you mentioned at this session tried to become part of the rule of law, and they could no longer have their own small armies and administrations on the ground. So the counts in the indictment or the statements in the indictment, saying that the government tried to centralise power for -- there were a million people living on the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One and a half million. Can we have the next page in English. And please read point 2, where it says "AD-1."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government has reviewed its obligations stemming from the conclusions and standpoints of the Assembly of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." What did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I said point 2 under AD-1.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government has looked at the steps that are necessary to introduce central authority in the republic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the discussion? You can read it all.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To that end, it has been concluded there should be an immediate public debate on the proposal decree on modes of carrying out the work of ministries or republican organisations outside their headquarters."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And go on. What would be agreed?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The meetings would focus on district organisation and also to shut down any legal para-state and other organs."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page. The next page in Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is there a schedule here on attending meetings in the districts, and who should go where, so that they can explain in these districts what a state actually is and how government should function; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As someone from Herzegovina, I was sent to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And please tell us where it says: "Discussion was held ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Debate was held on how to improve the government in present conditions with inadequate road, telephone, and other links in the field." The Serbian page is gone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please bring back the Serbian page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "A debate was also held, how to make the work of the government more efficient under present conditions with inadequate road, telephone, and other links with the field. It was concluded that larger centres should form units of certain ministries, acting as their forward services, to implement adopted laws and policies, and propose new laws or amendments to existing laws on the basis of their experience."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, let's round this off. Do you agree, and we've already mentioned that, that in the 1990s people came to power who had never been in power before and who, for 45 years, had been considered as the opposition and people who are not able to participate in government?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was a one-party system, and people came to power who had never participated in government before or held any kind of position of power, who had not been members of the Socialist Party, and that was the only party for 50 years in the former Yugoslavia. And these were the first democratic multi-party elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They were held in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the basis of your experience from the administration, were these two factors -- or three factors: namely, people in government without experience and knowledge; the war; and the breakdown in communications? Did that make chaos apparent, chaos that could not be controlled in any way?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please explain what you mean? Until the beginning of the war, or after the war started, the first months of the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first year of the war.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my opinion, no one thought that there would be a war. Once the war started, there were conflicts everywhere, in every part of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So at one point in time, there were armed conflicts throughout, from Una and Sava to Neretva, Trebisnjica, and all the way up there to Mrkonic Grad and Bihac. There was general chaos and commotion. All roads and communications were interrupted, and I think that both the people and the government lost their heads at that point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have AD-21 now in Serbian and in English. One more paragraph, please. AD-21. In the Serbian version, it's page 8 -- or 9, rather, in e-court. In English -- yes, we have it in English too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: AD-21, can you tell us what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government reviewed the current political and security situation in Foca and Bratunac. It was assessed that the situation in these municipalities was extremely complicated, and it was stated that necessary steps should be taken in order to prevent conflict and protect the population."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In that connection, the government believes that the possibility of imposing martial law should be looked at, in other municipalities as well, in order to bring order and avoid conflicts that could have broader negative consequences."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that Serbs and Muslims lived there at this point in time, that they are in direct contact, that conflicts may even escalate?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, both Foca and Bratunac were multi-ethnic towns, with equal shares of Serb and non-Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And at this time, end July 1992, both communities were living there together, they had already been fighting in conflicts, and the government had already taken some steps to prevent further conflict?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you rephrase, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To be more precise, is this the first time that the possibility of imposing martial law is being mentioned at a government session in order to prevent conflict, or is it for some other reason?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proposal before the government is to impose martial law to prevent conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was it not already admitted? Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D452, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 193, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the minutes of the 45th session. The one before was the 43rd session?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the 7th of August.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see AD-8 in both languages. [In English] Reference 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see in 3 that it deals with the operation of the power supply system. The transmission network is damaged. On page 3, it says the electrical company is tasked to let the other side know that the Serbian side would also use the power supply system for purposes of war, as they had been doing, if they continued to damage installations. Now, AD-8, can you tell us what the conclusion is in AD-8?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government considered the problems in the republic regarding the enactment of administrative regulations by various municipal and republic organs, which are not in conformity with the law. "In this regard, the government has decided that all ministries inspect all the enactments that had been passed during the war in order to remove any irregularities within an agreed time-frame ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see number 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you give us an explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The government decided that Vice-Prime Minister Milan Trbojevic and Minister of Justice Momcilo Mandic should assist in providing qualified staff for military judiciary organs."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D453, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D227, please. It's 65 ter 17664. The 65 ter has a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, we mentioned that the central authorities were not able to replace presidents of municipalities, but they did try to address the mistakes the latter had made mainly out of ignorance, and they sometimes abolished their decisions. We don't have the right document. It's 65 ter 17664. Do you remember that in the early days, there was a good president of municipality in Bijeljina, one Mr. Jokovic, and his error lay in his inclination towards paramilitary units, and I had to go to Bijeljina to ask him to resign, and Mladic demoted Mauzer, turning him into a simple private soldier, whereas he had been a major before? Now we need, actually, 1D227. This is not the right document. Do you remember that this was the first time a president of municipality was successfully persuaded to resign, and Mladic demoted Mauzer to a private?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember these activities of yours, and I don't remember what Mladic had done, but I know that this president of municipality, Jokovic, had turned over military barracks to paramilitaries, and that was the problem in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right, and that's the reason why we forced him to resign, and Mauzer was turned into a simple soldier. Now, tell us about this telegram from the Presidency of the Serbian Republic BH? In fact, it was already Republika Srpska, but we didn't have the stamps yet.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on your constitutional authority, you reversed the decision of the municipality of Bijeljina, dealing with military issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Point 2?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You ordered the civilian authorities to investigate the personal responsibility of the officials for passing illegal decisions during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And to report back; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to report on what they had done.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I tender this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember it was the constant complaint of the army that civilian authorities were interfering with command and control, and do you agree that it was a vestige of the former system of national defence and social self-protection, wherein the president of municipality was also commander of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what these were vestiges of, but I know that according to the Law on Territorial Defence under the Communist system, the president of the municipality was commander of the Territorial Defence. And these problems that the army had with municipal authorities are something I know nothing about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 65 ter 4214. Can this document be admitted, the previous one, the telegram?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D454, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One matter, Mr. Mandic. Do you, by any chance, know whether Territorial Defence still existed after the establishment of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of my knowledge, as of the 12 May 1992, the Territorial Defence did not exist, because the army was established then, and Ratko Mladic was named commander of the VRS. That was at the session of the Assembly in Banja Luka. From that time on, there was only the regular Army of Republika Srpska, from what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need 65 ter 4214.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, let me ask you: Do you remember that these municipal territorial units were only placed on the 19th or 20th May under the command of the army, but they continued to be called by their municipal names and they continued to rely logistically on municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know about the Law of the Army, they had to be made part of the regular army. But who financed them and whether it was the municipal authorities, I don't know, because the central authorities did not have the budget. So it must have stayed within the budget of the municipalities, as far as finance and supplies were concerned, but they had to be -- become part of the regular Army of Republika Srpska, according to the Law on the Army.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 1D212 for a moment, and then we'll come back to this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember our explanation why logistics should not be centralised? The reason was that municipalities would be more inclined to provide for their own children than to some unit they didn't know?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the government did not have the budget to finance that, and the municipalities that were under Serbian control, which were under Serbian control even before the war, had their own funds and budgets to feed the army, and, finally, also the police and the municipal administration. I believe that was the main reason why financing was left up to the municipalities, because up at Pale, we had nothing until the government was properly set up, until cash-flow started to run, until the establishment of everything that makes a state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this letter from Major Stankovic from the unit in Doboj. Read the title and the first sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is 27 July 1992, and the heading is "Report on the Attitude and Conduct of Individual Political Structures and Mandarins of Individual Socio-Political Communities Regarding the Establishment of Military Police Battalions": "In keeping with the order of the superior command, we have taken steps to establish and organise a united military police in the entire territory of Operations Group Doboj."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have this translated. Could you read the paragraph that begins with "Objective"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The objective of this organisation, in the spirit of your order, is to do away with all local and private military police units which are not accountable to anyone."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D455, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A witness here said that it took two years to establish. Do you agree that the army could not be set up and become operational on the 19th of May suddenly; it took time to place everything under a single command? Does this document testify to that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The formal conditions for establishing the army were created by 19th of May. However, after that time it took a while to pass the bylaws and implement these regulations on the ground. Now, how much time and how it was done concerning the army, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now come back to 65 ter 4214, the one we had before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the cover page for the verbatim record of the 20th session of the Assembly of Republika Srpska held in Bijeljina on 14 and 15 September; correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get page 9 in the text; English page 10. Page 9 in Serbian. I think it's page 9 in the document. Page number 9, the pagination of the document itself. The only thing here is that the prime minister and several ministers attended consultations, and at each of these consultations the demand -- sorry, the complaint was made that the authorities, the government, are not functioning properly. We need pages 15 and 16 in English, and page 15 in Serbian. In English, it must be towards the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please find the passage where it says: "We should be happy there were no executions by firing squad." In English, it reads: "I must say that very often some municipal officials ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, we should look towards the bottom of the page, and maybe it straddles page 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's in the upper part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: "I must say at the level of lower-ranking officials, clerks on the border." Do you mean that part: "There are many unpleasant surprises"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you read the passage where it says: "I have to say ..."?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean: "In fact, we have to be happy that there have been no executions so far"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Two sentences before that.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I have to say that very often some municipal officials have acted unlawfully, in ways that even deserved arrest and punishment."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this the right page in English, or maybe we need page 15. Your Honours, have you found it? [In English] "I must say ..." [Interpretation] It's halfway down the page, and we need the same page in Serbian back. [In English] "I must say it often happened that some municipal officials ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you go on, Minister?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: " ... acted unlawfully, in ways that deserved arrest and punishment. This is something we have to emphasise at this Assembly session and perhaps even sanction, and find a way for the Presidency to take a stand in such cases between two sessions of the Assembly. Namely, we should consider ourselves lucky that there have been no executions so far. But in future, there will be arrests and punishment. This Assembly is the legislative body whose duty it is to protect the law; will have to take note of this and give us authorisation. Even if we do not declare a state of war, we will have to straighten things out in certain municipalities of vital importance to use vigorous measures."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This was on the 14th and 15th September. The president of the Presidency is asking that the Presidency be given powers to take vigorous action vis-a-vis local authorities?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say there have been no executions, you mean to say that you didn't punish local Serbs. And you refer to the state of war, and you say that even without declaring a state of war, you need these powers in order to punish perpetrators of serious crimes in the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 18 in Serbian, and English also 18, top of the page. "How to ensure ...," the very beginning. It's the very beginning in English, and over here it says -- actually, we'll have to find this for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to have a look at line 4, Minister. Just have a look at that, and then we'll move further down.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 18?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 18, line 4: "I would like to ask General Mladic to present our military situation," et cetera." And then I said --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I would like to ask you not to repeat anything in this discussion. Let's move on directly to this objective, how to ensure the functioning of the authorities, how to make sure that profiteers and hoodlums do not undermine the authority of the authorities. Believe me, we found chaos in places where there were no authorities."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Further down: "Authority ...," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The authority of the authorities has hit rock bottom, but that happens all the time."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But we have some reports. Can you find that part: "Such strategically important places, like the Drina, the authorities of the central government, these guys in Bratunac ..." Have you found that? It's somewhere around the middle: "We have reports ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes: "These guys in Bratunac are very honest but they have no authority, they are not in power. When you translate 'authority,' it means the authorities or government. The authorities must have authority, and there can be no compromise. We must put our foot down and tell them to fuck off, use the police, and if you can't use your own police, call us and we'll send a special unit which will make arrests and restore order."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Further on?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "There is not a single municipal president who is able to do this unless he respects himself and unless we all contribute to him being respected."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that Brano Grujic testified in Belgrade about that in the proceedings that were held against him, that once they came to see me and they told me what the situation was concerning the Yellow Wasps, and then I asked Stanisic and Karisik [as interpreted] to send a special unit to arrest them because the local forces could not arrest them, as stated here in this paragraph? Was that the model that we applied?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now have page 49 in Serbian and page 47 in English. 49 in Serbian, 47 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Not to be narcissistic, this is Mirko Mijatovic talking, not me. Do you know who Mirko Mijatovic is?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he's an MP from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you look at this portion, where he says -- yes, it's the second paragraph. In English, it's also the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I would just like to say something very briefly about the functioning of the civilian authorities, where I think the problem lies in many municipalities. The government has, indeed, passed regulations, but we do not have developed mechanisms to implement them. I think that something constructive has to be done in order for that to happen. I have heard criticism of the commissioners. I am a commissioner of the Presidency for a large number of municipalities, and I don't know whether I have been of any use or not. But I can tell you of the following experience: that not a single representative of the government ever visited those areas. I'm not criticising anyone. I personally trust the president and many members of the government, but this contact has to be established with government representatives, at least between people working in the government and those who are on the ground."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have Serbian page 56 and English page 53.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Again, it's my own words. I can only be myself. Line 10 from the bottom in English. In Serbian, let's see: "Tonight we have to clarify certain matters here."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tell me roughly where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In English, it says: "We are responsible ..." Now we're going to find it --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "If necessary," you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Tonight, we have to be given that kind of authority ..." Yes, two or three lines. In English, it's line 10 from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We have to clear this thing up tonight. We must be given -- we must be given the authority to be able to replace and arrest, begging your pardon, a stupid municipal president. We are still faced with self-management, but still have the problem of self-management. This person cannot do this, the other person cannot do that. Self-management was designed to prove to you that something cannot be done and to prevent you from doing anything."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do I not ask, later on during this session, that the Presidency be assisted by being given greater authority in order to make arrests, and the legislation that is in place is a remnant of self-management?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the President of this honourable Trial Chamber asked me about this, I explained how a municipality president can be dismissed and that it did not depend upon the wishes of the government and the Presidency. It is the local parliamentarians, local MPs, who appoint such a person. He is responsible to them, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serbian page 73; English, 69.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is mid-September, and there is this fight going on in the Assembly for establishing effective government; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that things culminated at that point in time, that is to say, the struggle between the local and the central authorities, and that this led to major problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have a look at this. Jovo Mijatovic is speaking, and he says: "We ...," et cetera. Can you find that? I'll look it up in English, and you can look it up in Serbian. Zvornik is being referred to, and that will be the easiest way of finding the section that I've looking for: "At one point in time in the municipality of Zvornik ..." In English, can you find the word "Zvornik"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At one point, and I said this in Zvornik municipality several times, we were at a point where we practically had a municipal army, municipal police, and municipal administration, a state within a state."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next sentence too, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I hear that this is also the case at regional level in Eastern Herzegovina, that there are instances of regional organisation at all levels."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This assessment, made by Mr. Mijatovic, this is Jovo Mijatovic from Zvornik, does that correspond to what you knew at the time?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Serbian page 73; English, 69. Well, the English one can just stay there, because we are actually dealing with Professor Koljevic's remarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you testified in the Stanisic case, did you confirm that you did not know this man who was speaking, but that he was saying the same things that you knew about? Did you know this Mijatovic person?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. "Professor Koljevic," can we find this in Serbian, line four or five of his remarks. In English, it says: "On behalf ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm surprised that you don't know Mr. Mijatovic, because the Prosecution mentions him and says that you and I were involved in this joint criminal enterprise together with him. But let's leave that aside now. Minister: "Yesterday we did ...," or did not -- no, no, just a moment: "Yesterday, we ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Yesterday, we had a difficult day. We had to face our biggest mistakes and weaknesses, the truth of what things were like on the ground rather than what we would like them to be, and on television and at this Assembly, we have to present things. We are at the initial stage of these discussions. I would like to appeal to your honesty and openness."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Political"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Political," yes: "... the most political matter at this time, the centralisation of government and command for general well-being."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How about this sentence: "Because ..."?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Because local strongmen are a major problem for us. That is the main problem why the authorities are not functioning properly, why government is not functioning properly."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that in line with what you knew?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have Serbian page 88 and English page 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, these are your own words, page 93 and 88. You were still minister in mid-September; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have "Professor Zukovic" on my screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 88 in the text, itself, and it's 91 in English. Serbian, 88; 91 in English. It says "Momcilo Mandic." That's what's written there. Can we have -- this is some kind of new numbering of pages. Can we have English 91 and then 88, "Mandic." It should be Mandic's remarks. No, it's not this one either, no. Can we find Mandic's remarks, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: From what I hear from the Court Deputy, it's time to take a break. And after the break, we'll see Mr. Mandic's statement at the time. We'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we begin: Mr. Karadzic, you stated, during your question to Mr. Mandic, that Mr. Mandic was listed as one of the participants in the joint criminal enterprise. Over the break, I tried to read through the indictment, as well as the pre-trial brief, but I couldn't find Mr. Mandic's name. Could you clarify that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's not important. We can come back later on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but in any case, Mr. Mandic's name was probably dropped from the indictment when he was acquitted in Bosnia. But it does involve a huge number of people, paragraph 11 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But I would like you to be more cautious when referring to specific names as members of the joint criminal enterprise. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. At paragraph 11 of the indictment, it says that: "Radovan Karadzic acted in concert with other members of this criminal enterprise, including ..." And then the name of Momcilo Mandic is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My apologies. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that here or somewhere else, Zuca is also mentioned, and we arrested Zuca at the request of the municipal authorities, and a special unit was sent for that purpose from Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted into evidence, as well as the session of the 14th and 15th of September. I will desist from this part. But if this entire session has not been admitted, I believe that all the documents will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D456, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we now have 65 ter 201.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, we are still in September, and this is a session of the government. It doesn't say who attended it, but I'm sure you'll be familiar with item 1, AD-1. Can you describe to us what was discussed at this session?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a session of the Government of Republika Srpska of the 21st of September, 1992, where current issues of state and national interest were discussed, starting from the current situation and relations in the republic and further afield. Activities and measures to be undertaken were pointed out. Special attention was paid to consideration of the issue of the organisation and functioning of the state organs in the republic, the state of the economy and its revival, as well as organising the banking system in the republic and making it functional.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have the next page, please, in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And look at item 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can read this to the end.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Within this framework, special attention was paid to the situation and the measures and activities to be undertaken in the Bosnian Krajina. "After an extensive and comprehensive discussion, the government adopted the following conclusions: "1. The government shall energetically exercise its constitutional and legal functions, using all means of a law-governed state, in organising and exercising power in the republic. The government shall, where it is deemed necessary, propose to the Serb Republic Presidency the introduction of martial administration in certain areas of the republic, including companies, organisations, and institutions."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we now look at conclusion 12 in both versions. In the Serbian version, it's on the next page, and in English, it's also on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us about conclusion 12?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It was concluded that the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of Defence, in co-operation with the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, shall prepare and adopt regulations and unify their implementation in order to protect the property of persons outside the Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And 13. It refers to your ministry.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next page in Serbian, please. Only 13.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 13: "The Ministry of Justice and Administration is tasked with immediately preparing regulations on political organisation in the republic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Minister, that at the proposal of the prime minister, I suspended the work of the Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that other parties took advantage of this and began to organise themselves and became active in the areas left or abandoned by the Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does point 13 refer to the fact that the Ministry of Justice should organise political life, that is, how parties can organise themselves and be registered?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, let me ask you the following: If the purpose of government in Republika Srpska was to commit crimes, to expel Muslims and Croats, if that were the case, would not the government be happy that there was chaos on the ground, instead of trying to establish order?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat that the government did not insist on chaos and lawlessness, but, on the contrary, when the Serbian state was established, there was already chaos on the ground, and the government was trying to deal with this situation and introduce the rule of law.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D457, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have in e-court 1D234. 1D234.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And while we are waiting for it: In the previous document of the 21st of September, the government was considering the possibility of proposing to the president of the republic, that is, the Presidency, the introduction of martial law?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, or martial administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, in some places. Well, here, the minister of defence, at that time Colonel Subotic, was sending to the president of the republic something. So can you please tell us about this document? And here it says: "... and because of the serious threats, the whole system, and because of the danger of disintegration of the system, I propose ..." Can you tell us what it goes on to say, if you can see it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't see it to read this. It's all faded, it's very pale.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the original be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you read points 1 and 3, since these are the ones that have been translated?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence is addressing the president of Republika Srpska: "The introduction of martial law on parts of the territory of Republika Srpska": "1. Having in mind that in some parts of Republika Srpska, the political and security situation has escalated because of the activities of paramilitary units and para-state organs and institutions, and that the legal state organs and other authorities are not carrying out their work in line with the Constitution and legislation, and with a view to defence, and because of noncompliance with the decisions of the government and other organs, I propose the introduction of martial law in the following municipalities: Bijeljina, Centar Sarajevo, Ilidza, Ilijas, Hadzici, Novo Sarajevo, Stari Grad Sarajevo, Sokolac, Pale, Rajlovac, Vogosca and Zvornik. "3. Military administration," or, rather, "martial law in the municipalities from item 1 will be imposed until the reasons for the introduction of martial law are removed. "Minister Colonel Bogdan Subotic."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we mark it for identification, Mr. Tieger, pending the full translation of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI D458.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, this was on the 20th of October, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 20th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D232. I believe that we do not have a translation, but we will present the document with a few paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This was on the 10th of October. Before the minister of defence proposed this to me, the minister prepared mandatory instructions on the tasks of the organs of military administration, republic state organs and other subjects. Have I read this out correctly?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date is the 10th of October, and this was compiled at Pale. May we have page 10. The next number 2. This is the last page. I would like to see page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger, we have translations; not in e-court, but in hard copies. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have page 2 in Serbian. Page 1 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister -- could you put page 1 on the ELMO and then page 2 so that everyone can see what this document is. Thank you. Yes, we have it. Can you tell us about the part that's been marked in red?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the page you see now.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well: "1. The organs of military administration, in co-operation with the republican state organs, shall carry out administrative, professional, and other jobs according to the Constitution, laws and regulations based on the law. Legislative, administrative and other organs of administration are to be transferred fully to the military administration."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page, please; in English as well, probably. [No interpretation] [In English] The lower part. Point 1 -- 1.2. 1.1 is "Defence," and 1.2, it seems to me that it is not translated. [Interpretation] That page is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what they are doing in the Ministry of the Interior. Just tell us, briefly, what happens in case of military administration with internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They take over the entire -- all the competencies of the police, from investigating the most serious crimes to traffic control. They take over police affairs in full.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the last line: "Repressive measures ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Taking repressive measures against groups and individuals who make it impossible to carry out law enforcement or disrupt the political, economic, and legal system. And, as required, imposing curfew and restricting movement."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please. In English, it's 3. 1.3: "The judiciary and administration."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Ensuring completely functional --"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: It is wrongly translated. 1.3 looks like "Sphere of Defence and Administration," but it should be "The Sphere of Judiciary and State Administration."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell us what happens in this area, your field of work, under military administration?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our competencies, not only in terms of military judiciary, but also civilian judiciary, are transferred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the point is to maximise efficiency?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All administrative functions of the state are taken over by the military administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And number 3?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Priority dealing with reports for misdemeanor and criminal proceedings by the military administration and republic state agencies through summary procedures ..."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot see where the witness is reading from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last item?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Gradually enabling and putting into operation regular organs of state administration, executive and parliamentary bodies, in co-operation with the competent republic organs."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to 1.9. [In English] 1.9. [Interpretation] This deals with town planning, housing, and utilities, construction, surveyor and property-related legal affairs. Read the highlighted part, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Eviction from illegally-squatted apartments and residential buildings, recording damage inflicted on housing and other buildings," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How about property rights?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ensuring property rights, in keeping with the current legislation ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the rest of that sentence?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Serbian be scrolled down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Ensuring property rights, in keeping with the current legislation, and temporary ban on sale of real estate."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To whom does this eviction provision apply?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the Serbs, who moved unlawfully into vacant, abandoned houses and apartments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this last provision: "Ensuring property rights ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That applies to non-Serbs in the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Their property rights should be enforced and guaranteed; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the government had already imposed a ban on sales of real estate during the war so that no one should profit from these circumstances in buying property from Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that decree, with the force of law, was passed banning exchanges and sales of real estate until the war ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But under those circumstances, the Serbs had lost -- the Serbs in Croatia had lost both the property they owned in Croatia and property that they acquired in exchanges in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about such cases in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1.14, please, "Refugees and humanitarian aid."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Refugees and humanitarian aid": "Updating records and dealing with the status-related issues of refugees; providing for refugees in a more lasting way; establishing checks and controls to prevent any abuses of aid to refugees and humanitarian aid."
