utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next page?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Providing proper conditions for the return of refugees currently in other areas in the republic or outside the republic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And ...?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Full co-operation with agencies in charge of refugees."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this was signed ...?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By Bogdan Subotic, the minister.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you like it to be marked for identification, given that some pages are missing in the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think that's the appropriate approach under these circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI D459.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now get 1D233, to cast a brief glance at this document about the tasks of military administration; the same date, the same ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read the first page so the parties can be informed? And the Prosecution probably has a translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence passed this document. It's the Rules of Organisation and Mission of Military Administration.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the page -- the bottom of the page to see the date. I believe it's the same date as the last document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 10 October 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you interpret for us paragraph 2? So these are the rules binding the parties to take certain action?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Roman numeral I are general provisions?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Article 2, the defence minister defines military administration, and he says that it implies taking over entire authority and powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "... under the circumstances involving massive armed activities, unlawful conduct, and for other objective reasons where the constitutional and legal order has been disrupted"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the definition of military administration.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I would like you to give us next number 4. [Interpretation] Can we have Serbian page 2. Article 4, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Article 4?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Supreme Command, as the highest body in the system of military administration in the republic, shall establish military administrations in municipalities and other communities. "Military administration commanders shall be appointed by the defence minister. "Unified military administration may be established for areas including two or more municipalities."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Article 10, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 15?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 10: "The bodies of military administration, in co-operation with republican state bodies, commands, and army units, and other entities, are duty-bound to remove and eliminate all the causes and reasons for which military administration was imposed, within the time-limits established in the relevant document."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now Article 15?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In carrying out the duties and tasks in their area of work, the bodies of military administration shall have jurisdiction to use the police and may also require the engagement of army units when that is in the interests of defence," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Article 16, "Final Provisions"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes: "These rules shall enter into force on the date of promulgation and shall not be published in the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska, but will instead be made available to the users, together with the decision to impose military administration. "Defence Minister Bogdan Subotic."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Scroll down to see this. Thank you. [Interpretation] May this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D460, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D1984, please. Not translation, I'm afraid. Perhaps the OTP has a translation. In any case, it's very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So read it in full.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pursuant to Article 7, paragraph 5, of the Law on Defence, and in view of the fact that it's impossible to establish civilian authorities, the president of the Presidency of Republika Srpska hereby adopts the decision to impose military administration." Article 1: "Military administration is hereby imposed on the territory of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Brod." Article 2: "The military administration shall carry on in its tasks and duties pursuant to the law and other regulations of Republika Srpska, following the organisation and issuing of tasks prescribed by the defence minister." Article 3: "This decision shall enter into force on the date of adoption and shall apply pending the establishment of civilian municipal authorities, but not longer than four months." Signed: "President Radovan Karadzic."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is one example of such a decision that we laid our hands on. It concerns the municipality of Brod, Bosanski Brod, and it's the same date as the previous document. On the same day when the minister proposed it, I imposed military administration. May this document be admitted, please? Could the transcript please reflect that the witness confirmed what I had said in my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, did you confirm what Mr. Karadzic said earlier on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, on the same day this order was made, the same day when the minister of defence made that decision. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D461, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D19895, please. Could we have that in e-court, 1D1895.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please interpret this for us? You don't have to read it out. It's not that -- 1D1985. It's not that document. Could this be placed on the ELMO. Oh, no, right, this is the document I wanted. Minister, can you tell us briefly what this is? This is obviously one of a series of documents from the minister of defence. Can you tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that previous document, it says that the minister of defence appoints the head of the military administration, and this is an example of such an appointment. The minister appointed Lieutenant-Colonel Dragutin Mikac for the municipality of Brod, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what does paragraph 2 say?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The head of the Military Administration of the Serb municipality of Brod is in charge of the Military Administration and is duty-bound to ensure the carrying out of tasks and duties established in the rules on the organisation and tasks of Military Administration," and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 3: "Reports on the work and functioning of the Military Administration. The Serbian municipality of Brod shall be submitted by the head of the Military Administration, to the minister of defence, every 15 days, and, if necessary, more often that that."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Signed: "Bogdan Subotic"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the document be admitted for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D462, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D1986, please. It's all in this same series from the same municipality. 1D1986.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may suggest a time expedient, one which I've discussed with Mr. Robinson. It may be more appropriate, and certainly more expeditious, for the Defence to Bar-table the remainder of these series of documents. We now know the context. They can indicate the particular relevance. The Prosecution -- and the providence. The Prosecution could respond. The Court will have more information, and we will move through this process faster, and the accused will have more time to deal with Mr. Mandic on the subjects about which he can provide specific elaboration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. I was wondering the point of putting these documents to the witness, again, with which the Prosecution has no disagreement. These kinds of documents may be the ones that will be put to the witness to take a look at overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And also then subject to later Bar table motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would have asked to be heard on the suggestion of presenting documents to the witness for -- to append his signature on the basis of some -- well, on the basis of the suggestion the accused made about some familiarity. We wouldn't know anything about that. I would think, for the reasons mentioned earlier and for that reason, the Bar table submission would be far more preferable. The Court would have much more information from both the Defence and any responsive information from the Prosecution, plus the possibility of hearing any additional -- of having the opportunity to see any additional documents that the Prosecution, in this case, or the other side when the Prosecution makes Bar table submissions, may also consider relevant. And then with that information, the Court can decide what's appropriate to admit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now I see your point, Mr. Tieger. Do you have any observations, Mr. Karadzic? Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. I think we would be amenable in trying to do as much as we can through a Bar table motion, although we saw that the Bar table motion of the Prosecution didn't go too far when it first started, and so we think there's some risk, possibly. But with the Prosecution's position, at least -- we would be willing to take that risk and try to move to a Bar table approach with some of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The witness testified, in general terms, about the Military Administration, but there's no need to go through each and every document with the witness, while he was asking for further time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was going to make a very similar point, Your Honour, and I think you beat me to it, and that is: Whatever risk existed before, I think, has been overtaken by the fact that we now have a great deal of contextualisation for the submission of these documents as well as other issues which have been contextualised during the course of this witness's examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then this would be the last one that I will be dealing with in this way, because it belongs to this series, and we'll see about the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, is this the 6th of February, 1993? The military administrator, Lieutenant-Colonel Dragutin Mikac, is reporting about the establishment of civilian authorities in the municipality of Brod, and he is informing the minister of defence about that; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read the first paragraph, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I hereby inform you that in the municipality of Brod, on the 5th of February, 1993, civilian organs of municipal authority have been constituted. Through the election of Assembly bodies and organs, the requirements have been met from Article 3 of the decision of the president of the Presidency of Republika Srpska, number 01-1788/92 of October 10, 1992, for abolishing military administration in the municipality of Brod."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you go on? Can you read the part further down?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was submitted to the authorised organ of the 27th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D463, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that criminal reports were not reflected in the transcript, "Criminal reports."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read this out once again: "Criminal reports ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Criminal reports, with evidentiary material, have been taken out of the register and were sent to the authorised organ of the 27th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the military administrator filed criminal reports with regard to all crimes, and charged that 27th Motorised Brigade with dealing with this further?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably from that motorised brigade or from another organ of the military judiciary.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This has been admitted; right? Has it been admitted? 1D2079, could I have that, then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us see what happened in your own ministry on the 21st of October, 1992, with a view to establishing the rule of law. 1D2079. Do we have that or shall I have a copy placed on the ELMO? Some ERN number is -- yes, that's it, right. You don't have to read the preamble to us. Could you just tell us what kind of decision this was that you passed?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had to do with the appointment of the republican administrative inspector, Ms. Milena [phoen] Vucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to us what that means? What does this administrative inspector do? What is his or her job?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The job involves going to see local authorities and examine the legality of the activity of local government in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can it be MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, why was this necessary?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because regulations were being violated in the domain of local government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Couldn't have this been done in other ways? This inspector actually had to move about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, an inspector has to see what bylaws say and other documents adopted by municipal assemblies and other local organs, to see the extent to which regulations are being violated, those that were passed by the Assembly and that the government was supposed to work on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be MFI D464.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, it seems to me that in your testimony in the Stanisic case, or at some assembly, you said that these local princes would sometimes even establish local prisons that did not belong to the system of the ministry, or, rather, the legal system; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that did happen, and we established that here as well, that this happened when the war started in Bosnia-Herzegovina, or, rather, in the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 135, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If I may intervene once again, Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Mandic, I heard your evidence, before the war, after the war, or when the war started. When did the war start? What incident do you call as the start of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Armed conflicts in Bosnia and Herzegovina started on the 6th of April, 1992, when Bosnia-Herzegovina was recognised by the European Union. According to all experts and in different cases, especially in General Galic's case, when seven experts were heard, including Robert Dole [as interpreted], it was established that the armed conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina started with the armed conflict in the territory of the city of Sarajevo, on that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree, Minister, that incidents before the 6th of April primarily had Serb victims? The 3rd of March, Bosanski Brod, then the 25th and 26th of March, Bosanski Brod and Sijekovac and the Neretva River Valley, Travnik and so on, then Serbs were moving out of Livno, all of that happened before the 6th of April. Do you agree that that was also a war along with attacks from Croatia by the Croatian regular and irregular army?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are considered to be inter-ethnic incidents and clashes that do not have the characteristics of an armed conflict, that is to say, a war, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 135, please. May I inform all the participants that now we are moving on to the topic of prisons and prisoners of war. I'm afraid this is not the right document. 65 ter 135, please. It is not 1D135; it is 65 ter 135. This one will be very interesting, too, because it speaks about the links that the Muslim government had with various international Arab intermediaries or brokers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a session held on the 6th of August; can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page; in English as well, the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So could you please have a look at this?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work of the commission was discussed, the work of the Commission for Investigating War Crimes Committed against the Serbian People in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in the former Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Conclusion": "The Commission for Investigating War Crimes commited against the Serb people will start working, even if it is necessary to replace the members of the Commission. The treatment of --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Prisoners of war"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... prisoners of war detained in prisons in Serb territory was discussed. The prisoners should be divided into three categories: those captured on the front; those who took part in arming and operations of the Territorial Defence of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina; and those who assisted and financed Alija's army. It was pointed out that we should abide by international conventions on the treatment of prisoners of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, do you agree that prisoners of war are only those who participated in enemy combat activities in one of the three ways described here and that there is no mention of civilians?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any civilians being mentioned in this text, only three kinds of prisoners of war; immediate participants, those financing, and those assisting arming.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page in Serbian and keep the current page in English. The next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read us the whole page: "To that end ...," and then the conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To that end, the completely humane treatment of prisoners of war is advised because they are in prisons and not in concentration camps. In wartime, payments for their food, clothes, hygiene, guarding, and so on are made at our expense. "Conclusion: The Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina will be ordered to examine, through its municipal branches, the behaviour of all civilian authorities and individuals guarding prisoners of war. The information will be passed to the MUP," that is, the police, "which will pass it on to the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." And the signatory is "Radovan Karadzic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This was on the 6th of August; is that right? That was the date on the first page?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 1 of both versions, the English and Serbian, so that we can check the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the date is the 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D465, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have D100 - I think it's already been admitted - just to remind ourselves what I wrote to the prime minister. D100. It's been admitted as D100. I hope there is a translation. Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a letter sent from the Presidency to the government, to Mr. Branko Djeric, and it says: "Dear president, I am enclosing copies of the reports I have just received regarding the state of prisoners in Manjaca and Bileca. In relation to these reports, I have sent a letter to Mr. Cornelius Samaruga, the president of the ICRC, and General Ratko Mladic. "I expect that the government, through the ministries of law -- through the ministries of justice and internal affairs, based on the reports, will take immediate measures for the improvement of the living conditions in the prisons that are operated by civilian authorities on our territory."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This has already been admitted. May we have the next document, please. We are now dealing with the topic of prisoners of war and the institutions detaining them. May we now have 65 ter 11512.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Minister, that a large number of Muslims responded to Alija Izetbegovic's call for general mobilisation issued on the 4th of April, 1992, that a huge number responded?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that on the 4th of April, Mr. Izetbegovic made a public proclamation of general mobilisation, but I'm not informed as to how many Muslims responded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But do you accept the assessment of their generals that 70 or 75 per cent of their soldiers fought wearing their civilian clothes, at least in the first year?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't want to intervene much, but in this case I think the witness has indicated he doesn't know, and now he's being asked whether he has any reason -- whether he's accepting a proposition made by, presumably, officials with whom he's not familiar. I'm not sure how that advances the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The second question seems to be related to a separate issue, as to the issue of wearing civilian clothes, so I let it go. Mr. Mandic, can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have already answered this question. I know that at the beginning of the war, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not have uniforms that were all the same and that a large number of people wore civilian clothes. I've already said that two or three days ago. But as to what numbers or what percentage of those were in civilian clothes, I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page. The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 9th of August, was this signed on behalf of Mr. Djeric by the deputy prime minister, Trbojevic, and can you tell us about this decision?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I explained this decision in the Stanisic case, where I have fully accepted my testimony in that case, but I will repeat that. At your request and pursuant to your letter of the 7th or 8th of August, as we saw, a commission was set up to visit all the places for which it was learned -- it was found or suspected that there were persons being detained. So when Avlijas, from the Ministry of Justice and Administration, and Goran Saric, from the Ministry of the Interior, as professionals, expert in those issues, were appointed to that commission, one of them went to the Krajina, the other one, Mr. Avlijas, went to Central Bosnia, and Goran Saric, the third member, went to Herzegovina, to visit all the places and all the municipalities for which there was reason to believe there were local prisons or places where non-Serbs were being held. So the government responded immediately.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D466, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D1902. 1D1902. While we are waiting for it to come up: This is a document issued by the Ministry of the Interior, dated the 10th of August. I don't know whether we have a translation. Yes, we do. I will ask that you be handed this decision. I'm not sure this is the document. 1902, it's dated 1992. It's something military from 1995, so 1D1902. This is the document in Serbian, yes. Now, do we have a translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is the next day. The minister of the interior, pursuant to the decision of the government, is issuing instructions to the centres in the places listed here. Can you tell us what the minister is ordering?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister of the police is issuing an order that the detention and holding measures shall be applied exclusively within existing regulations, and he tells the chiefs that they shall be personally responsible for the lives of people who are being held and detained. And he is calling for the prevention of any form of abuse in that area. The premises were people are being held or detained must fulfill basic requirements of hygiene and health. And in item 2: "The security of collection centres shall be the direct responsibility of the Serbian Army, and if they do not have enough men for these duties, it shall therefore be necessary to engage members of the reserve police for these tasks and to place them at the army's disposition." And it's signed by Mico Stanisic. Those who do not comply with this order shall be disciplined.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D467, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1D219. This is the 14th of August. So four days later, the 14th of August, the minister's order here is being made operational. I hope we have the translation. Yes, we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So to avoid reading the whole document, can you tell us who is making this operational and how?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was sent to the chiefs of the regions, the one -- not this one, but the one by the minister, and now the chief of one of the regions is establishing commissions to visit the municipalities, tour the municipalities, and establish what the situation is in these municipalities as regards the detention of persons by the police and holding them in custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I think that the names of these people are mentioned in reports we shall see later on, but what you have told us is the gist of this document?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So Vojin Bera, Vaso Skondric, Ranko Mijic and Jugoslav Rodic are members of the commission. Can you read the explanation -- the statement of reasons to us?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The chief of the Security Service Centre of Banja Luka ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the page be scrolled down in English or the next page opened? We need the end of the document in English. Yes, this is it.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the chief, pursuant to the order of the minister of the interior of the Serbian Republic, the chief of the Banja Luka Security Centre has issued this decision on the establishment of the commission to visit the municipalities of Prijedor, Boskoski Novi and Sanski Most, and he gives him the tasks listed in this decision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it's Mr. Zupljanin who issued this order as soon as he received the minister's letter; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D468, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have 1D1905.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So when it's zoomed in, can you tell us what sort of document this is, and who signed it, and what it means?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recognise the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But can you tell us what this document is about? It's another order; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an order repeating the order: "... to all security services centres, public security stations, and their organisational units to act exclusively in accordance with the law, with MUP responsibilities, and with the regulations of the International Law of War and International Conventions when dealing with prisoners of war and the civilian population refugees. "The ministry is to be informed immediately of the existence of potential unofficial prison camps and to any behaviour towards prisoners of war and refugees violating legal provisions and international conventions. "It is necessary to immediately initiate the collection of intelligence and documentation on individuals violating the existing regulations and acting contrary to our orders." And they are to be reported to the relevant prosecutors' office. And it's signed by for the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D469, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we get 1D2044. And now we rely on our learned friends to produce a translation, if they have one. The page ends with numbers 527.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Minister, if I'm not mistaken, this is a status report, and refugee-related issues, collection centres, evacuation, et cetera, and it refers to the document from Mr. Zupljanin. It says on the 14th of August, the commission of Sanski Most -- Prijedor, Bosanski Novi and Sanski Most hereby submits this inspection report, and it first deals with Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems we will get a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, 17874.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tieger. This is the cover sheet in Serbian, and we now see the English. Can we turn to the next page in Serbian. Now, the first sentence, please, and the second paragraph, and the next page in English as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The armed conflicts began in Prijedor municipality on 24th of May, 1992, in the broader area of the Kozarac settlement between the forces of the Serbian Republic and Muslim extremists, and then spread to other places in the municipality."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll deal with that another time. Now we are interested in this inspection report. The next paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "During these clashes, the Army of Republika Srpska captured a large number of members of enemy units and other persons who had been found in the areas of armed conflict, and a number of citizens leaving their homes sought help and protection."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next paragraph, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In order to deal with this problem, the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor municipality decided to organise reception and accommodation of such persons in Trnopolje and that prisoners of war should be held for processing in the building of the Keraterm work organisation in Prijedor or in the administrative building and workshop of the iron ore mine in Omarska."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, read the sentence that contains the date "24 May 1992."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "As of 24 May 1992, a large number of Muslim citizens of both sexes and all age groups sought protection in the centre. There are currently around 1500 citizens of Muslim and Croat ethnicity in this centre."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One more sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The number of people in the centre varies. There are no special records kept, since the citizens are free to come and go as they please."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is halfway through the last paragraph. I hope you found it in English. [In English] "24th of May." [Interpretation] It's halfway down the last paragraph. Thank you, Minister. Now, can you go on? And in English, we'll probably need the next page. The next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Around-the-clock infirmary has been organised in the centre, and activists of the Red Cross, the municipal authorities, and the army are providing the citizens with aid in food, clothing, and other things. In the centre, the citizens have organised themselves, and they obtain and prepare food and other essentials. The area used for this purpose is not fenced in, and there is no interrogation of citizens in the centre. Army troops stand guard outside the centre to secure it against any threat from the extremists outside."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is your knowledge about Trnopolje consistent with this report by this police commission?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about Trnopolje or Manjaca, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will also hear evidence from foreign witnesses that Trnopolje was a self-organised centre. Do you know that in Prijedor, after over 3.000 fighting men were captured, investigation and interrogation had to take place in another building because the police station couldn't hold them?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please. We stay on the same page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2: "Pursuant to the decision of the Crisis Staff, mixed operative teams were established, including representatives of national, public, and military security, with a task to conduct an operative processing of all the captives and establish the degree of their personal responsibility in armed combat."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this problem -- the army and the police created a joint team to question all the people captured and established the degree of their liability in armed combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it customary that documents are compiled in every individual case, documents and records that would show why someone was released or detained in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In keeping with the Law on Criminal Procedure, a statement has to be taken in writing, and the entire legal procedure has to be followed to establish whether there are any grounds for releasing or detaining someone. The police could hold a person legally for 72 hours - I don't know about the military police - and within that time-frame they had to be either processed or transferred to the Public Prosecutor's Office for further processing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page in both versions: [In English] "... in the municipality quickly spread to most of the settlements ..." [Interpretation] "However, armed conflict quickly spread throughout the municipality."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please read this passage that begins with the words: "According to available documents ..."?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "According to available documents and lists, between 27 May and 16 August, 1992, a total of 3.334 persons were brought to the Omarska Investigation Centre. They had been captured by the army in combat or had been found in places where hostilities had occurred, or had been brought in on the basis of the results of the operative processing in the investigation centre."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And go on, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "After completing their investigations, and depending on the results, the operatives divided all the captives into three categories, according to the degree of personal responsibility in the armed insurgency."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So peace was somehow maintained until the 24th of May, and the armed insurgency occurred only then?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "27 May."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 27th of May is when they were brought in, but the armed insurgency happened on the 24th?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first category, a person suspected of the most serious crimes, who were directly involved in the organisation and -- of the armed insurgency and the insurgency, itself. The second category are persons who are suspected of organising, aiding, abetting, and financing and illegally supplying arms. Category 3, persons who are captured and brought in from areas where they had been fighting, but happened to be there --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "... who happened to be there because they were unable to withdraw to a safe place because of their own extremists. During the investigation, no evidence was found that they had in any way taken part in the armed rebellion."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "For each category and each individual, the operatives compiled documents and evidence. After that, 1.331 persons were transferred to the Manjaca Army Camp, 1.773 to the Open Reception Centre in Trnopolje, while 179 are still being investigated in the Omarska Investigation Centre."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, do you agree that 1.773 persons were freed from further investigation, and that is 57 per cent; right? What I mean to say is: More of them were freed and volunteered to go to Trnopolje than the total of persons who were placed in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you rephrase that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this report show that more than 50 per cent were freed from further investigation?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that there were more of those who went to the Open Reception Centre in Trnopolje? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, do you see that there were 3.000 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, do you agree that those who were transferred to Trnopolje were freed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's why I asked Mr. Karadzic to rephrase, because it says they were placed in the Open Reception Centre, Trnopolje. I was only looking at the figures, but whether it was an open or closed reception centre, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, I'm noting the time. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have to raise a scheduling issue which I think may be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's the question I was going to put to Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you've spent so far 19 hours and 15 minutes with this witness. If we would stick to the 20 hours we originally allowed to you, you would have only 45 minutes left, and you should be able to conclude your cross-examination by the end of today. In any event, for planning purposes, and even for your planning purpose, the Chamber wishes to know how much longer you would need to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was hoping, Your Excellency, that I would have at least two sessions tomorrow. You see how many areas we have yet to cover. We finished with the struggle with the municipal authorities, investigations in prison. We have to deal with the refugees and their return. What we are doing now, Trnopolje, Omarska, Manjaca, and other prisons, we need to go through documents and to see what the powers of the president were, because the indictment frequently alleges that the president was able to carry out investigations. And this witness, since he is a lawyer and he was a minister of justice and administration, is able to tell us exactly what the president was able or was not able to do. He is such a precious witness to me, and I would appreciate it, really, if I could have at least another half hour to get Mr. Mandic to assist us in getting a full picture about Sarajevo; who was where, who was holding which positions, who was fighting against whom, which part of the population was situated where, et cetera. Mr. Mandic can be very helpful in this issue. I don't think that we should sacrifice this opportunity of hearing a very well-informed witness to expediency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will give its ruling when we resume at 10 past 1.00, after a 30 minutes' break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber has considered your request and decided that you will have two hours tomorrow. I'm afraid, Mr. Tieger, that may complicate the scheduling matter on your part. That means the next witness should be interposed by the second-next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, we were trying to deal with all the permutations that might follow the current schedule, so let me raise a couple of issues, if I may, Your Honour. As it turns out, it appears that we -- that arrangements can be made for an interpreter for Thursday, but we would need to know that. So that would mean, among other things, it would be extremely helpful if the Court could advise us, at the first opportunity, of the length of anticipated cross-examination for Mr. Abdel-Razek.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct. I think originally we anticipated -- we understood that interpreters would only be available Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, but it looks like CLSS can make arrangements for one additional day. One of the reasons I raise that is that might make it possible, therefore, given the schedule tomorrow, it looks like we wouldn't finish Mr. Mandilovic, rather than putting him over entirely, you know, for many extra days, we could complete his testimony on Monday if we factored in the length of anticipated cross-examination and the availability of one more day for the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the Chamber will be able to give you the time-limit for Mr. Karadzic's cross-examination of those witnesses coming by tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I understand the arrangements -- we have a specialised interpreter, an Arabic interpreter involved, and so I gather, from the information we've received, that those arrangements have to be made by the close of business today. So while I hesitate to push the Chamber on this issue, I think that's an answer we need at the first opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'll give it a try, to give you that estimate before the end of today's business.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I was advised by the Court Deputy that the Registry has kindly agreed to sit on Monday from 1.30 to 7.00. So unless the parties have a problem, we'll sit in that way on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I suppose the only thing that occurs to me is since the interview of the witness is expected for Monday -- we haven't been able -- we haven't been able to reach the witness because he's en route, so we don't know what answer he'll give, but it does occur to me that the earlier the court time commences, perhaps the less willing the witness might be to engage in an interview that concludes immediately before he's supposed to take the stand. But I leave that to the Court and to the Defence, primarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll finalise the matter tomorrow. Thank you. Let's continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, since I was not given as much time as I had hoped for, allow me to summarise, and could you please follow and see whether that's it. The other participants can do that as well. You said that documentation, accompanied by material evidence, was compiled for every person, and that is why some persons were transferred to Manjaca and others to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It is too fast for interpretation. We don't have the figures.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't follow you because you spoke so fast; in particular, the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Those operatives," that paragraph. We've dealt with that already in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm just trying to say that documentation had to exist then. They confirmed that documentation did exist and that on the basis of these previous proceedings, 1.331 individuals were found to be combatants, transferred to Manjaca, and 1.733 to the centre, while 189 persons were still being processed. Do you agree that this documentation was, indeed, established and that it should be before this Court?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this document. These are police documents. I can only give an interpretation on the basis of the text I see here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We asked the OTP, and the OTP was convinced that there were 10 batches. Now I'm going to ask the Trial Chamber to encourage the OTP to get these 3.000-something investigation documents to see why certain persons were deemed to be combatants and others were set free. 57 per cent were set free. Could we please have those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, does it say here that there were 11 Serbs as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't want to intervene and waste Mr. Karadzic's time, but I suggest to him that he doesn't do so also. If he has a 66(B) request to make or something of that nature, we can do it in proper form rather than taking time during the course of this witness's examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, agreed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think we already asked for that, and that the response we got was that this was in the first 10 batches. They did, indeed, kindly provide us with those 10 batches, but it's not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, then, even more inappropriate, Your Honour. Can we proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's not waste, I think, precious court time. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, does it say that there were 11 Serbs there and also that only 179 persons remain, and they would be dealt with within seven days, that the investigation would be over with in seven days; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is stated here, 11 Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph, it says that on the basis of what the chief said, the investigation of the --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 179 persons remaining will be completed at the latest within seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next paragraph -- or, rather, the next chapter speaks about the moving out of citizens from the municipality of Prijedor. Can we have the next page in Serbian, please. It says here that families of these extremists, 4.000 to 5.000 of them, had left earlier on, probably because they had received information that there would be conflicts, whereas the others went through regular procedure and asked to be allowed to leave in order to go to Croatia and Europe; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this text, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking whether that is what it says in this text, in this police report. I understand as minister of justice, you didn't know have to know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Mandic. I didn't recognise -- yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just wanted to note that we're continuing now in a series of questions, asking this witness whether the document says what anybody in the courtroom, or, for that matter, anybody outside the courtroom can see what it says. I don't think this adds any value, and it is a waste of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I can't agree more. We can read the documents if we admit it. And you can raise the points during your submission. Ask a question the witness is really aware of.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I address the Defence in this respect, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, these are documents that are police and military documents from 1993. This is the first time that I come across them. If you have some documents or questions where I was personally involved, where I participated, where I can shed some more light, whereby I can present the truth to this Court, then please put questions like that to me. This is the very first time I see these police orders, then this military jurisdiction, and so on. I really feel useless. Can I be somewhat more useful? It seems to me that I'm sitting here in vein.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we just have the last page, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether these people did that exactly or whether this was a usual type of police report. That's the only thing I wanted. So can we just identify the date in both versions and the signatures of these persons who you probably know or you have heard of them, at least?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Drljaca, the chief, signed this, and I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, I have something different. Page 16. Page 16, Vojin Bera, Vaso Skondric, Ranko Mijic, Jugoslav Rodic, on the 18th of August, 1992. So you were still minister, but not of the police, but minister of justice?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 16, right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. So this is a report for the area of Prijedor. This is a commission that was established by the chief of the Centre of Security Stations of Banja Luka in accordance with the order issued by the minister.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The English version only has to do with Prijedor; whereas the Serbian, it's Prijedor, Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sanski Most, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Has this document already been admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D470, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have a request. Could the translation be adjusted? It should be the translation of this document rather than just of this police report signed by Simo Drljaca. 1D1851, could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, while we're waiting for this: Have you read Professor Koljevic's diary?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. What I wish to say now is recorded there. Do you remember that Muhamed Cengic asked, through Biljana Plavsic, that I allow Muslims from Trebinje to move out of Trebinje, and that I refused that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the former Deputy prime minister of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Muhamed Cengic, asked for permission for Herzegovinians of Muslim ethnicity to move out, but I don't know what happened with regard to the actual decisions. I know that he publicly called for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but I refused it. We have a document here before us. These are instructions of the Party of Democratic Action. It says here: "Party of Democratic Action, Trebinje." That is the addressee. We see all of that. We all see this document. In this document, instructions are provided -- Hasan, the other Cengic, actually, the clergyman and the SDA secretary. Could I have the next page, please. Instructions are being provided to Muslims to go to Montenegro. Now, do you remember that after they left, the Muslims, the SDA, asked that Trebinje be given to them, in terms of maps, because Trebinje had been a victim of ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document earlier on, Mr. President, and I know that Hasan Cengic, a hodja from Ustikkolina, who was the secretary-general of the Party of Democratic Action, asked his countrymen to move out of certain parts of Eastern Herzegovina in order to achieve his objective; namely, he wanted the international community to be angry at the Serb municipalities that gravitated towards Montenegro and, in part, Serbia as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say here all of your -- "Restitution will be made for all of your property when we achieve our goal and we will know how to put the right price on your sacrifice, a sacrifice that all of the Muslims in the world expect from you"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I saw this document before.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D471, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall corroborate this by using Professor Koljevic's diary. Can we have 65 ter 196, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it Mr. Koljevic's diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, I wanted -- I wanted to make a point, that once again I ask to be advised, if possible -- I know we're moving at a reasonably quick pace, but I hope the Defence is aware of which documents they've notified and which they haven't. And if they can advise us when they are producing a document that's not among the 1200-plus documents that's on the list they provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this minute was not informed?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, that was a reference to the previous document, which we saw for the first time just as it was placed on the screen before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, but it's the rush that has to be blamed for this. We've up-loaded over 2.000 documents. Had we had a bit more time, we would have done all of that, but we also believe that the Prosecution is aware of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, is this the 19th of August, so everything seems to be happening in August? This was a government session held in August; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of the very few government sessions that was closed to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see, closed to the public. And the previous report, wasn't that on the 18th of August, and then the government looked at it already on the 19th? So look at paragraph 2. The government was actually reviewing the report of the commission, so it's the first number 2 that you can see there?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes: "The government reviewed and adopted the report of the Commission on Touring Collection Centres and Other Facilities for Captives in the Autonomous Region of Krajina, along with the assessment that this report realistically portrays the situation in these facilities." This was submitted to the government within 10 days, and the government accepted the report, approved it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that, as it says in the last sentence, there are no concentration camps in the Krajina? I have this document somewhere. That's what the government told me. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This record was forwarded to you in the Presidency, and it seems to me President Djeric informed you of this also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't have to read it all. Can we look at page 2 in both Serbian and English. The signature is of President Djeric and Lakic, the government secretary; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May it be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D472, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have D101 - it's probably been admitted as D101 - simply to refresh our memories. This is a document -- no, this is not it. D101, or 1D244. But it's been admitted, 101. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Minister, that in the first sentence here it says that: "Pursuant to our document of the 13th of June," which is long before the visit by the ICRC, "we issued an order, and now we reiterate ..." "we reiterate the order," that's been underlined again, "we order," and then there are some paragraphs dealing with the topic we've been discussing. Can you tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a second order, it's a repeated order. It's dated the 13th of June, 1992, or, rather, it's pursuant to the first of the 13th of June, 1992, and this one is on the 19th of August, and it orders that all entities honour their commitment and comply with International Humanitarian Law, especially the 3rd and 4th Geneva Conventions; to issue instruction to all combatants and all employees of the Ministry of the Interior to respect Imprisoned individuals, civilians, medical institutions, private and public places, the emblem of the Red Cross, and the people and resources of the United Nations."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we've looked at items 3 and 4 with Witness Doyle, as regards the handover of property, so we needn't go into that, but can you please look at point 4 because it refers to this topic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To immediately take steps to improve conditions in all prisons within the Serbian Republic in accordance with the recommendations given by the International Committee of the Red Cross during its visit to these places."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have the last page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first order of the 13th of June was before the ICRC visit, while this one already refers to it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you read the last point?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The general standpoint is that every army and police organ of the Serbian Republic is obliged to provide every assistance for members of the International Red Cross, and any violation of the International Humanitarian Law is obliged to carry out a vigorous investigation."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have 2092, 2D2092 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 1D2092.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a resume from a working meeting of MUP personnel in Trebinje, so all this is taking place on subsequent days -- on successive days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It doesn't say so here, but is the date the 20th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have page 6 or 7 of the document. In English, it's page 9. Unfortunately, we can't look at everything. In English, it's page 9.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The assessment of the chief of the Sarajevo Security Centre, the Crime Investigation Service, regardless of the lack of --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I don't see it in English. Oh, yes: "The Sarajevo CSB chief ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Sarajevo CSB chief is of the opinion that the Crime Prevention Service has, despite the shortage of professional staff, significantly increased its productivity in the last period (366 reports of serious crimes submitted). The efficiency regarding war crimes has been improved. The incidents of car theft and theft of other kinds of property have also been significantly curbed thanks to the operational and preventive measures taken ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So this is a report saying that by the 20th of August, activities had been stepped up to discover the perpetrators of war crimes, especially -- of crimes, especially war crimes?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now have the next page in Serbian and page 10 in English. "In Bijeljina --" "The situation in Bijeljina" in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read this about Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The situation in Bijeljina is relatively satisfactory, but in truth is much worse than at first glance. The problem with the Muslim section of the population is compounded by the arrival of Muslim refugees and the return of those who had left Bijeljina before, influenced by Mr. Karadzic's and Mr. Panic's recent statements. This population includes a number of Muslim extremists, and it is believed that a large number of Muslim citizens --" Could we scroll down a little bit in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Own weapons," is that it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: " ... Muslim citizens own weapons."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Mr. Panic at the time was the prime minister of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this report from Bijeljina say that after my appeal and Mr. Panic's appeal for the return of refugees, refugees did, indeed, return to Bijeljina, but among them there were a number of extremists?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's all there in the report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. There are many interesting points in the entire report, so I recommend everyone to read it. May it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D473, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it our general position that refugees go back whenever it was safe, whenever it was possible? Do you know that at any time, in any round of negotiations or conferences, we constantly held the position that refugees have the right to return and to have their property reinstated? Did we always work for that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, you always advocated that returns could -- refugees could return to those places that were free of combat and their property would be restored to them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, 65 ter 01131. 65 ter 01131.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it a dispatch from the Security Services Centre, Banja Luka, of 20th August?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it now Mr. Zupljanin forwarding, again, an order from Minister Stanisic to public security stations, that is, subordinate commanders?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now read briefly what Stanisic ordered and Zupljanin forwarded or passed on?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the CSB, public security stations in localities are ordered again to act strictly within the law and the international conventions, and to take control and deal with irregular prisons, and to ensure compliance with the international conventions with regard to the treatment of refugees and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, the last sentence?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It is necessary to proceed without delay, to gather information and documentation, in order to submit a criminal report to the competent prosecutors' office." That's again the same dispatch that Stanisic had sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But he's now reiterating it, he says, "I order again"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we admit this, but all the witness did is just reading out some passage in the document. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D474, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, may I say that the minister worked first on the police force, then he was briefly, for a month, in our ministry of Republika Srpska, and at this time he was minister of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a normal, standing activity of the Ministry of the Interior in law enforcement and ensuring regularities? Was that an activity that was discussed at Cabinet sessions?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The activities of Minister Stanisic, in terms of law enforcement and insistence on legality, were constant, and he reported regularly to Prime Minister Djeric and to the entire Cabinet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does this document have a number already? Can we now get 1D1903. 1D1903. The Serbian version is the right one, and the English one too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you take a look at this telegram. Four days later, Minister Stanisic sent this to all security services centres and all public security stations, so the security services centres directly subordinated to him and the security stations subordinated to CSB?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he sent this dispatch to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He notifies that the Ministry of Health asked something of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of Health asks that information be collected on detention camps, prisons, and collection centres in the territory of the republic, and he asks, from CSBs and public security stations, to provide the following information: the name of the place where a camp or collection centre is located; 2, the name of the person who ordered that this institution be established; 3, the name of the person who ordered people to be brought in to these detention camps, centres, et cetera; 4, the number of people in captivity, and lists containing their personal information; 5, the number of persons arrested, those in temporary detention separately from convicts, and lists of their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does our language and our regulations -- do they make a distinction between arrested persons and convicted persons?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
